My exact replay /workspace/branches/audit_period_graph.py computed the cell images [11,17], [7,11], [5,7], [3,5], [12,14], [10,12], [6,10], [0,6] in the same coordinates. Because image endpoints are partition boundaries, a transition between cell interiors must cover the whole target cell; isolated endpoint hits are handled by the boundary orbits. The four graph components are simple cycles (0,7), (1,4,6,3), (2), (5). Every infinite itinerary eventually stays on a simple cycle, and contraction of its inverse branches makes an infinite cyclic itinerary a single periodic point. The exact replay solved each cyclic affine equation: the (0,7) candidate is on the boundary, not an interior orbit; the other solutions are the stated four-cycle and the two fixed points. This distinction is slightly obscured by the phrase 'interior graph cycles' in the frozen proof, but it does not alter the list or the boundary argument. Nested survivor sets exclude all other periods at smaller a; the old orbits survive even at a=2/5 and the eight-cycle requires a>=7/17. This proves the zeta formula at all orders, not merely the finite-period diagnostic. The compact restriction is continuous; the survivor is countable by finite preimages of finitely many orbits, and invariant measures give full mass to the periodic points by recurrence. The dimension and topological entropy are therefore zero.
